trials.name: INVOKE-2
trials.primary_endpoint: Disease Progression as Measured by the Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score
trials.results_summary: The Phase 2 trial failed to meet its primary endpoint; AL002 did not significantly change the CDR-SB score versus placebo and showed no treatment effects favoring AL002 on secondary endpoints. It also notably induced amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).

trials.population: Participants with early Alzheimer's disease who completed the INVOKE-2 study
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety and Tolerability as Measured by Number of Treatment-expected Adverse Events (TEAE) and Treatment-related Adverse Events (AEs)
trials.results_summary: The open-label extension was terminated because the parent study (INVOKE-2) failed to meet its primary and secondary clinical endpoints.

trials.population: Healthy participants and participants with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Evaluation of safety and tolerability of AL002 measured by number of subjects with adverse events and Dose Limiting Adverse Event (DLAEs)
trials.results_summary: First-in-human data showed AL002 was generally safe, well-tolerated, and successfully demonstrated target engagement in the CNS by decreasing sTREM2 and increasing relevant biomarkers.

trials.primary_endpoint: Safety: Incidence, severity, and seriousness of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
trials.results_summary: The trial was completed in healthy volunteers, but efficacy and detailed safety outcomes have not yet been published in a peer-reviewed format.

trials.population: Healthy Adults and Patients With Alzheimer's Disease
trials.results_summary: Phase 1 is listed as completed but formal clinical results have not yet been read out or published.

related_evidence.description: Results of the AL002 Phase 2 INVOKE-2 trial reporting failure to meet the primary clinical endpoint and the occurrence of ARIA.
Publication of AL002 Phase 1 clinical trial data and preclinical evaluation showing safety and target engagement.

evidence_assessment: The document's preclinical discovery of TREM2-dependent Disease-Associated Microglia (DAM) sparked significant clinical interest in targeting TREM2 to clear Aβ plaques and restrict Alzheimer's disease. Based on this hypothesis, multiple TREM2 agonists (e.g., AL002, DNL919, VG-3927) entered the clinical pipeline. However, the most advanced candidate, AL002, recently failed its Phase 2 efficacy trial (INVOKE-2), showing no benefit over placebo on cognitive decline (CDR-SB) and frequently inducing amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA). This major clinical setback strongly challenges the translational validity of the hypothesis that pharmacological TREM2 activation can safely restrict neurodegeneration in human Alzheimer's disease.
discrepancies: While the document argues that TREM2-dependent DAM activation has the potential to restrict Alzheimer's progression based on transgenic mouse models, the human clinical record shows that the first-in-class TREM2 agonist (AL002) failed to slow cognitive decline in Phase 2 and was associated with significant adverse events (ARIA), leading to program termination.
